caption: Causative Structures
body: The subject causes another person or thing to perform an action. In informal conversations, “get” can replace “have”.

lines: I had my room painted last week.
She will have her passport renewed.
I got my roof repaired last week.

body: To emphasize that the object has the responsibility to do something, like an order.

lines: My brother has his children pick up their toys after playing with them.
I have my assistant take regular breaks throughout the day.

body: To exercise authority or control over the object to perform an action.

lines: The parents made their children study math all day.
He made me eat all the vegetables even though I dislike them.

body: To give permission to the object to perform an action.

lines: My mom finally let me cook with her.
They will never let me go in these circumstances.

body: To influence or persuade someone to perform an action.

lines: I got my cousin to lend me his tablet.
Jeremy got the investor to invest in his company.

body.text: The four structures can be used in all tenses, and also with modal verbs.
